text.title: WebSocket Design Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable signals to a rule from content/01-core-rules.xml: first the protocol choice, then the protocol-hygiene gates walked in order. The skip-this-methodology branch is always reachable.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the workload require sub-second server push AND client→server traffic?

conclusion.verdict: use Server-Sent Events; simpler, HTTP/2 multiplex, resume built in
use HTTP long-poll or move to a stateful tier
short-lived and small; SSE or polling fits and the protocol ceremony does not pay back
use WebSocket with envelope, heartbeat, reconnect-jitter, pubsub fan-out

section.title: Protocol hygiene gates
section.p: Walked in order once the tree above chose WebSocket. Each is blocking.

conclusion.verdict: BLOCK — adopt {v, type, channel, id, seq, ts, payload}
BLOCK — attach a JSON schema per type and validate on both ends
BLOCK — wire application ping/pong at 25–30 s with a ~90 s timeout
BLOCK — full-jitter exponential backoff capped at 30 s
BLOCK — bound the queue and name the shed policy
BLOCK — single-use signed token with TTL <= 5 minutes
BLOCK — emit a truthful RFC 6455 code so the client can decide reconnect vs give up
APPROVE — wire the fan-out bus and run the reconnect-storm load test

text.example: Multi-client live cursor product → versioned envelope v=1 → heartbeat 25s — disconnect after 2 misses → reconnect full-jitter capped 30s → Redis Pub/Sub for fan-out → bounded queue 100 msgs.

Long-lived, 100k concurrent → envelope versioned → every type carries a schema → heartbeat present → jitter present → queue bounded at 1000 with drop_oldest → ticket TTL 300 s → close codes 1000/1001/1008/1009 emitted → APPROVE.
